description: Alliances, treaties and blocs for the Contractor faction pack, plus the full relations matrix (77 x 77, row = the faction's view of the column). Faction files keep their notable relations; this matrix is the single source of truth.

alliances.name: North Atlantic Treaty Organization
alliances.obligations: Article 5 collective defence: an armed attack on one member in Europe or North America is an attack on all.
alliances.notes: 32 members in 2026; 20 are in the roster. Finland joined in April 2023 and Sweden in March 2024. Non-roster members include Albania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, Hungary, Iceland, Luxembourg, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Portugal, Slovakia and Slovenia. tur is a full member but its relations with several allies (grc, the sdf issue) are strained; war_join for tur is still auto by treaty. Partner states are modelled in nato_partnership_for_peace, not here. Ukraine and Georgia are aspirants (2008 Bucharest declaration) with no accession timetable.

alliances.name: NATO Partnership for Peace
alliances.obligations: Bilateral cooperation programmes with NATO; no defence commitment either way.
alliances.notes: Roster participants only. Russia and Belarus are formal participants whose cooperation with NATO is suspended or dormant; they are left out for game purposes. Ukraine also has the NATO-Ukraine Council, and Georgia and Ukraine are NATO aspirants. Replaces the free-form tags nato_partner and nato_partnership_for_peace.

alliances.name: European Union
alliances.obligations: Article 42.7 TEU mutual assistance ('obligation of aid and assistance by all the means in their power'), without prejudice to the neutrality of some members.
alliances.notes: 17 roster members are full members. Candidates (member_status candidate): ukr and mda (accession talks opened June 2024), geo (candidate since December 2023, process de facto halted by the EU in 2024), srb (talks open, slow) and tur (talks frozen since 2018). war_join applies to full members only; aut and irl are militarily neutral and contribute non-military aid. Replaces the eu_candidate tag.

alliances.name: EU Eastern Partnership
alliances.obligations: EU association and partnership agreements; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Belarus suspended its participation in 2021 and is not listed. Armenia, the only member without candidate status, signed a Comprehensive and Enhanced Partnership Agreement and passed a law in 2025 to begin an EU accession process. Replaces the eu_partnership tag.

alliances.name: Five Eyes (UKUSA Agreement)
alliances.obligations: Signals-intelligence sharing under the UKUSA Agreement; no defence commitment of its own.
alliances.notes: Kind intelligence_alliance as named in the handoff sheet (not in the base kind list). Defence commitments among these five come from nato and anzus.

alliances.name: AUKUS
alliances.obligations: Trilateral security and technology partnership: Pillar I nuclear-powered submarines for Australia, Pillar II advanced capabilities. It has no mutual-defence clause.
alliances.notes: The handoff sheet suggested kind defence_treaty; AUKUS contains no mutual-defence obligation, so it is modelled as a strategic partnership. Defence ties among the three come from anzus and nato.

alliances.name: ANZUS Treaty
alliances.obligations: Each party would 'act to meet the common danger' in the event of an armed attack in the Pacific.
alliances.notes: The US suspended its ANZUS obligations toward New Zealand in 1986 over nuclear-free legislation (member_status suspended); the treaty remains in force between the US and Australia. US-NZ defence cooperation has since been rebuilt under the Wellington (2010) and Washington (2012) declarations.

alliances.name: Quadrilateral Security Dialogue
alliances.obligations: Diplomatic and security dialogue; no defence commitment.

alliances.name: US-Japan Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security (1960)
alliances.obligations: Article V: each party would act to meet an armed attack on territories under Japan's administration.
alliances.notes: US forces are based in Japan.

alliances.name: US-ROK Mutual Defense Treaty (1953)
alliances.obligations: Article III: each party would act to meet an armed attack in the Pacific area on the other's territories.
alliances.notes: US Forces Korea are based on the peninsula.

alliances.name: US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty (1951)
alliances.obligations: Article IV: each party would act to meet an armed attack in the Pacific area on the other. The US has stated that it covers armed attacks on Philippine forces, vessels and aircraft in the South China Sea.

alliances.name: Taiwan Relations Act (US law, 1979)
alliances.obligations: US law, not a treaty: the US provides defensive arms and maintains the capacity to resist force against Taiwan. No defence commitment (strategic ambiguity).
alliances.notes: Modelled at partnership level because there is no treaty; the US has no diplomatic relations with Taiwan.

alliances.name: US Major Non-NATO Ally designation
alliances.obligations: US designation easing arms sales, defence-research cooperation and war-reserve stockpiles; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: usa is the designating state; others are partners. Saudi Arabia was designated in November 2025. Taiwan is treated as a major non-NATO ally under US law without formal designation (member_status de_facto). Non-roster designees include Argentina, Bahrain, Brazil, Colombia, Kenya, Kuwait, Morocco, Thailand and Tunisia.

alliances.name: Collective Security Treaty Organization
alliances.obligations: Article 4 collective defence: aggression against one member is aggression against all.
alliances.notes: Non-roster members: Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. Armenia froze its participation in February 2024, has paid no contributions for two years and its prime minister said in August 2026 that Armenia will not return within five years; it has not formally withdrawn (member_status suspended, war_join never applies to it). The CSTO intervened in Kazakhstan in January 2022 but did not act for Armenia in 2021-2022. Replaces the csto_suspended tag.

alliances.name: Union State of Russia and Belarus
alliances.obligations: Treaty on Security Guarantees (December 2024), including Russian nuclear protection of Belarus.
alliances.notes: Russian tactical nuclear weapons are stationed in Belarus (2023).

alliances.name: Russia-DPRK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty (2024)
alliances.obligations: Article 4: immediate military assistance if either party is attacked.
alliances.notes: North Korean troops fought for Russia in the Kursk region in 2024-2025, and North Korea supplies artillery ammunition and missiles.

alliances.name: Sino-North Korean Treaty of Friendship (1961)
alliances.obligations: Article II: immediate military and other assistance if either party is attacked.
alliances.notes: Renewed automatically every 20 years; China's willingness to honour it in practice is debated, hence likely rather than auto.

alliances.name: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
alliances.obligations: Security and political cooperation; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in 2024. Non-roster members: Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan.

alliances.name: BRICS
alliances.obligations: Economic and political forum; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Full members in the roster: rus, chn, ind, irn, egy, are (plus Brazil, South Africa, Ethiopia and Indonesia). Partner countries (member_status partner): kaz and blr (since January 2025) and vnm (2025). Saudi Arabia's status is ambiguous: BRICS lists it as a member but Riyadh has not confirmed joining, so it is not listed here.

alliances.name: Commonwealth of Independent States
alliances.obligations: Post-Soviet political forum; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Ukraine stopped participating in 2014-2018 and Georgia left in 2009. Moldova has been leaving CIS agreements and is not listed.

alliances.name: Eurasian Economic Union
alliances.obligations: Customs union and single market; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Non-roster member: Kyrgyzstan.

alliances.name: GUAM Organization for Democracy and Economic Development
alliances.obligations: Political and economic cooperation; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Largely dormant at summit level.

alliances.name: Organization of Turkic States
alliances.obligations: Political and cultural cooperation; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Non-roster members: Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan. Observers include Hungary and Turkmenistan.

alliances.name: Shusha Declaration on Allied Relations (Türkiye-Azerbaijan, 2021)
alliances.obligations: Mutual assistance if either faces a threat or attack from a third state.

alliances.name: Mecca Joint Defence Agreement (Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, Pakistan, 2026)
alliances.obligations: Collective defence among the three signatories; on 5 October 2026 the partners agreed to activate collective-defence deployments in Saudi Arabia.
alliances.notes: Signed 7 August 2026, building on the Saudi-Pakistani Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement of 17 September 2025 (an attack on either is an attack on both). Recorded from the research in sau.json and tur.json.

alliances.name: Gulf Cooperation Council
alliances.obligations: Joint Defence Agreement (2000) and the Peninsula Shield Force; political and economic union.
alliances.notes: Non-roster members: Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman. The 2017-2021 Qatar blockade shows the limits of cohesion.

alliances.name: Arab League
alliances.obligations: Joint Defence and Economic Cooperation Treaty (1950), rarely invoked.
alliances.notes: Syria was readmitted in May 2023. Palestine is represented by the PLO/State of Palestine (pse_pa).

alliances.name: Abraham Accords
alliances.obligations: Normalisation of relations with Israel; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Non-roster members: Bahrain, Morocco (Sudan signed the declaration). Kazakhstan joined in November 2025, a largely symbolic step since it already had full relations with Israel. Egypt (1979) and Jordan (1994) have separate peace treaties with Israel, modelled as relations only.

alliances.name: Axis of Resistance
alliances.obligations: Informal Iran-led network: Iranian funding, weapons, training (IRGC Quds Force) and coordinated campaigns; no treaty.
alliances.notes: Syria left it with the fall of Assad (December 2024). Degradation by October 2026: hamas heavily degraded (Gaza war; ceasefire since October 2025, disarmament framework pending); pij heavily degraded; hezbollah degraded (2024 war, leadership losses, Syrian supply line lost; re-entered war March 2026, Israel occupies much of south Lebanon); iraqi_militias intact but under US strikes and Iraqi disarmament pressure; houthis the least degraded (joined Iran's 2026 war, Bab al-Mandab escalation September 2026); irn at war with the US and Israel since 28 February 2026. Terrorist members are hostile-only to the player; war_join here means 'surge activity', per game_rules.war_join.

alliances.name: Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS
alliances.obligations: Political coalition of 90 members (Syria became the 90th in November 2025); military operations are run by members, not the coalition.
alliances.notes: Roster members listed as far as verified; the full partner list was not re-checked line by line (phl and srb membership not verified, left out). sdf and krg_peshmerga are not members: they are partner forces on the ground (member_status partner). Syria's accession is a political declaration without military provisions.

alliances.name: Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition
alliances.obligations: Saudi-led counter-terrorism coordination centre in Riyadh; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Roster members from the original 2015 founding list. Qatar's status since the 2017 Gulf crisis is unclear and it is left out; Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger are members as states, but the sahel_aes faction is not listed.

alliances.name: African Union
alliances.obligations: Political union; the Peace and Security Council mandates missions such as AUSSOM in Somalia.
alliances.notes: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger (sahel_aes) are suspended after their coups (member_status suspended).

alliances.name: Alliance of Sahel States (Confederation of Sahel States)
alliances.obligations: Liptako-Gourma Charter (2023): an attack on one is an attack on all; confederation since July 2024 with a unified force.
alliances.notes: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger are modelled together as sahel_aes. africa_corps is a partner (Russian state contractor working for the juntas), not a member. The three left ECOWAS in January 2025.

alliances.name: Association of Southeast Asian Nations
alliances.obligations: Political and economic association; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Both claim parts of the South China Sea against China.

alliances.name: Joint Expeditionary Force
alliances.obligations: UK-led high-readiness force framework; no treaty defence commitment beyond NATO.
alliances.notes: Non-roster member: Iceland.

alliances.name: Nordic Defence Cooperation
alliances.obligations: Defence cooperation; no separate defence commitment (all four are NATO members).
alliances.notes: Non-roster member: Iceland.

alliances.name: Nordic-Baltic Eight
alliances.obligations: Regional cooperation format; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Non-roster member: Iceland.

alliances.name: Bucharest Nine
alliances.obligations: NATO eastern-flank coordination format; no separate commitment.
alliances.notes: Non-roster members: Bulgaria, Czechia, Hungary, Slovakia.

alliances.name: Weimar Triangle
alliances.obligations: Consultation format; no defence commitment.

alliances.name: Benelux Union
alliances.obligations: Economic and political union; no separate defence commitment.
alliances.notes: Non-roster member: Luxembourg.

alliances.name: E3 (France, Germany, United Kingdom)
alliances.obligations: Diplomatic format, chiefly on Iran's nuclear programme (snapback of UN sanctions in 2025).

alliances.name: Five Power Defence Arrangements
alliances.obligations: Consultation if Malaysia or Singapore is attacked; no commitment among the roster members themselves.
alliances.notes: Non-roster members: Malaysia, Singapore.

alliances.name: Group of Seven
alliances.obligations: Economic and political forum; no defence commitment.
alliances.notes: The EU also takes part.

alliances.name: UN Security Council permanent members
alliances.obligations: Permanent seats and veto power in the UN Security Council.
alliances.notes: Descriptive grouping with no alliance effect; rep_spill 0.

alliances.name: UN Interim Force in Lebanon
alliances.obligations: UN peacekeeping mandate in south Lebanon; the Security Council (August 2025) set the mandate to end on 31 December 2026, with withdrawal during 2027.
alliances.notes: Roster troop contributors in lebanon_south (kaz serves with the Indian battalion; deu leads the Maritime Task Force). Neutral: never side-locks and never joins wars. Peacekeepers appear on lebanon_south maps as neutral units.

alliances.name: al-Qaeda and affiliates
alliances.obligations: Pledges of allegiance (bay'ah) to the al-Qaeda leadership.
alliances.notes: Hostile-only to the player. Fights islamic_state_network wherever they overlap (Sahel, Somalia, Yemen). Terror networks never join wars; they surge activity (game_rules.war_join).

alliances.name: Islamic State and provinces
alliances.obligations: Provinces (wilayat) under the Islamic State's central leadership.
alliances.notes: The handoff sheet called this isis_network; the id already used in the faction files (islamic_state_network) is kept. isis covers the Iraq/Syria core plus the Sahel and Somalia provinces. Fights al_qaeda_network and afg_taliban.

side_lock.rule: Taking a contract against faction X locks the player out of X's contracts, and out of the contracts of every faction whose relation toward the client is -50 or below.
side_lock.duration_scaling: Scaled by contract severity (escort 3 days ... HVT kill or capture 10 days).
side_lock.exempt: Peacekeeping (unifil) clients and neutral humanitarian clients (che, aut, irl) never lock, and never cause a lock.
side_lock.terror_groups: Terror groups are never clients, so they never lock; working against them never locks anyone out except their own network.

war_join.auto: Treaty partners with war_join auto (nato Article 5, union_state, rus_prk_treaty, us_jpn_treaty, us_kor_treaty, aes) join the simulated war when a full member is attacked.
war_join.likely: Partners with war_join likely join with probability 0.6, raised to 0.9 if their relation to the victim is +70 or higher.
war_join.possible: Partners with war_join possible join only if their relation to the victim is +70 or higher (probability 0.3).
war_join.none: Never join because of this alliance.
war_join.member_status: Only full members trigger and answer war_join; suspended, observer, partner, candidate and de_facto members do not (arm in csto, nzl in anzus, candidates in eu).
war_join.terror_networks: Terror networks and the axis_of_resistance's non-state members never 'join' a war: they surge activity (more attacks and contracts against them in their theatres).

rep_spillover.formula: For reputation change rep_delta with faction X, each other faction Y changes by rep_delta * clamp(relation(Y, X) / 100, -1, 1) * alliance_factor.
rep_spillover.per_alliance: Each alliance's game_effect.rep_spill is its alliance_factor; when X and Y share several alliances, the highest applies.
rep_spillover.sign: Negative relations invert the delta: helping X angers X's enemies.
rep_spillover.scope: Whole matrix, weighted as above (default; open question).

player_trade.sellers: Only factions with player_trade.sellable true sell to the player: usa, gbr, can (decided), che and aut (Captain-confirmed 2026-10-10), krg_peshmerga basic kit (Captain-confirmed), plus the proposals in the remaining files (aus, nzl and several European states carry sellable true as proposals).
player_trade.requirement: A relation of at least +40 toward the player plus the faction's rep tier; che and aut (relation +15) are exempt as neutral arms markets that sell on rep tier only.
player_trade.never: Terror groups, cartels, rival PMCs and africa_corps never sell.

matrix_method.file: Value listed in the faction's own file (researched per faction).
matrix_method.mirror: Only the other faction listed the pair; the same value is used both ways and written back to the faction file.
matrix_method.override_or_rule: Neither file listed the pair: judged from real 2026 ties (explicit pair list), from group rules (terror groups, cartels, PMCs, non-state forces) or from shared alliances.
matrix_method.formula: Remaining state pairs with no strong ties: 10 + 35 * west(a) * west(b), rounded to 5, with floors of +60 for a shared defence treaty or military alliance, +50 for eu/gcc/five_eyes and +15 for sco/brics/arab_league/turkic/abraham_accords.
matrix_method.symmetry: Every pair agrees in sign and is within 30 points (most are equal).

proposed: game_effect values for every alliance (war_join, side_lock, rep_spill)
relations_matrix values filled by override, rule or formula (see matrix_method); file values are the factions' own
alliance kind intelligence_alliance for five_eyes (not in the base kind list)
Grouping of the terrorist groups into al_qaeda_network, islamic_state_network and the axis_of_resistance as game networks (memberships themselves are factual)
